arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Roysden argued that Congress created a high bar for federal evidentiary hearings under AEDPA.
Mr. Loeb argued that the statute requires a finding of fault to bar a hearing.
Chief Justice Roberts noted that excusing a default implies the right to present supporting evidence.
Justice Thomas questioned the utility of excusing a default without allowing evidence development.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of federal habeas review. It asks if a prisoner can present new evidence after missing state deadlines. The outcome affects the balance between state finality and federal oversight.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants a federal evidentiary hearing to present new evidence supporting his habeas claim.
the opposing side wants the federal court to deny the hearing because the state court barred the claim.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that excusing a procedural default requires allowing the prisoner to develop the underlying factual basis.
the opposing side argues that the statute only bars hearings when the applicant failed to develop facts through fault.
